result:
I changed search indexing so results follow the rule you gave, and rebuilds now produce exactly the allowed entries. I did not run the test suite; the only check was that `tsc --noEmit` reports no type errors.

- **Index writers:** the index functions in `src/server/services/search-service.ts` now check the whole parent chain before writing.
  - A project is indexed only while it is live.
  - An issue is indexed only while it and its project are live.
  - A comment is indexed only while it, its issue and that issue's project are all live.
  - Anything that fails the check is removed from the index instead of upserted. Comments now also carry their project id.
- **Archiving and restoring:** archiving an issue re-evaluates that issue and all its comments. Archiving or restoring a project re-evaluates the project, its issues and their comments. Issues archived earlier stay hidden after a restore because they fail the issue check. Comments and edits made later go through the same checks, so they can't slip in under an archived project. Reindex requests for comments and projects are now handled too; before, only issues were.
- **Rebuild job:**
  - `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` first deletes all of that org's search entries, then reindexes every project, issue and comment through the checked writers. Other workspaces' entries are untouched.
  - It now walks every page of projects, issues and comments, so large workspaces are covered in full.
  - The delete-then-reindex step needed a new function in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`.

If a rebuild fails partway, the workspace's index stays partial until the job is run again, because it clears the org's entries before reindexing.
